sentences.text: This early penguin featured a long, narrow beak and paddle-shaped wings.
The holotype fossil, which is the specimen the species is based on, was found in 1980 near the Waipara River in Canterbury, New Zealand.
Mayr and colleagues re-examined this holotype in 2018 and established the new genus Muriwaimanu for the species M. tuatahi.
A second partial specimen was later discovered by Leigh Love in 2017 within the Waipara Greensand.
Muriwaimanu is classified within the order Sphenisciformes.
Muriwaimanu was an extinct early penguin that lived in New Zealand during the Paleocene epoch.
It lived between 61.66 and 56 million years ago, spanning the Selandian to Thanetian stages.
Researchers suggest that Muriwaimanu may represent a transitional species leading to modern Antarctic penguins.
